title: Impact of a Radiologic and Immunologic Signature on Cerebral Efficacy of Treatments in Lung Cancers With Brain Metastasis
official: Impact of an Immuno-radiomic Signature on Intracranial Treatment Efficacy in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer With Brain Metastases at Diagnosis
summary: Non-small cell lung cancer frequently spreads to the brain, and brain metastases are associated with poor prognosis and limited treatment response. This retrospective study will investigate whether quantitative features extracted from brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), known as radiomic features, are associated with the immune characteristics of brain metastases assessed by bulk RNA sequencing. The main objective is to identify relationships between MRI-based radiomic signatures and tumor immune profiles. A secondary objective is to determine whether radiomic, transcriptomic, or combined radio-transcriptomic signatures can help predict cerebral progression during immunotherapy. The study hypothesis is that MRI-based radiomic signatures may reflect the immune environment of brain metastases and could provide a non-invasive approach for predicting treatment response.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older
* Advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer not amenable to local treatment
* At least one brain metastasis at diagnosis, surgically resected for symptomatic or high-risk disease and/or for diagnostic purposes
* Indication for first-line treatment with immunotherapy and chemotherapy
* Signed CHU de Bordeaux "one shot" form or receipt of the study information letter without opposition to participation within one month

Exclusion Criteria:

* Small cell lung cancer
* Resection performed for oligometastatic brain disease
* Oncogenic addiction amenable to targeted therapy
* Medical, psychiatric, or other condition preventing understanding of the study information or completion of the study
* Legal protection measure, including safeguard of justice, guardianship, or curatorship
* Deprivation of liberty by judicial or administrative decision
* Inability to provide consent
